decisions.advocate: Close the concern only after it is split: the file-scope half is provably right, but "`framework/` is out of scope" is currently carrying two unstated consequences — no gate ever runs this check before a pin bump, and the "nothing left at HEAD" rule has no committed source of truth.
decisions.decision: Closed as confirmed rather than assumed: `framework/` is root-excluded from every phase job's checkout via `plugin/ci/run_phase.py`'s RUNNER_EXCLUDES (`/framework/` in `.git/info/exclude`), and `git diff --name-status -M <merge base>...HEAD` lists only committed paths, so it structurally cannot appear in `check_ratchets`' input; the design's scope boundary stands unchanged.

rationale: Both verdicts agree the core claim is right: reviewer calls it a correctly scoped boundary, and advocate's own point 1 says framework/ can never appear in this check's input — no false positive, no false negative.

The stronger, checkable reason (RUNNER_EXCLUDES + diff --name-status's committed-paths-only semantics, verified in plugin/ci/run_phase.py:366-387) replaces 'assumption' with a structural guarantee, so the item closes rather than staying an open assumption for the owner to bless.

The advocate's other two points (pin/release enforcement timing for this change's own gate; whether the eval-case 'emptied at HEAD' rule reads git ls-tree or the filesystem) are not about whether framework/ is in scope — they are separate design/requirement gaps outside this one item.

Per the brief's limits, adding a requirement, accepting a risk, or deciding those two points is not available here; they park for the owner as their own finding rather than being folded into this concern's closure.
decisions.reviewer: Accept the assumption as correct: `framework/` is properly out of scope; no fix needed to spec.md or plan.md.
